question: How many UN member states will vote in favour of the annual TPNW resolution at the First Committee's 2026 action phase?

calls.reasoning: Recorded First Committee votes on the TPNW resolution: 122-41-16 (2018, L.24), 118-43-13 (2020, L.6), 121-44-12 (2025, A/C.1/80/L.18; GA plenary 119-45-12). The question background's '144 in 2024' doesn't fit this series (likely mixed up with another nuclear text), and the range was evidently built on it. The status quo is about 118-124 in favour, so the most likely 2026 count is about 117-125, below the 129.5 lower bound. Reaching 130+ would need 9+ new 'yes' votes in one year, which has never happened. Upward drivers like the Review Conference momentum are small. True belief: about 97% below range, but the declared below-range mass is capped at 0.5. In-range percentiles are conditional and sit near the lower bound. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market found.

The background's '144 (3 against, 30 abstentions) in 2024' cannot be the TPNW text, which faces a stable bloc of about 44 'no' votes, so the range is built on a misattributed number. Status quo for 2026 is about 118-125. Reaching 130+ would take a gain of 9 or more in one year, which has never happened. The Review Conference (Nov-Dec 2026) and a few new ratifications (e.g. Tonga) are small upward pushes. The true below-range probability is about 95%+, so p_below_lower is declared at the 0.5 cap and the in-range conditional percentiles hug the lower bound. calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the main factual point: the real TPNW First Committee yes count has been 118-124 since 2018 (121 in 2025), and the background's 144 refers to some other resolution. The minor factual dispute over the 2024 tally (124-43-14 vs 122-44-14) and its document number (L.24 vs L.37) could not be settled without web access. It makes no difference, because both readings sit well below 129.5. The remaining questions are judgment calls: how much mass to put below range (everyone is at the 0.5 cap) and where the in-range conditional percentiles sit. I carried forward a lower-bound-hugging shape similar to Runs 1 and 3, with a slightly wider top for the risk of resolving off a different text.
